newsitem.title: USA: Delgratia Mining faces second lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Delgratia Mining faces second lawsuit.

text.p: Investors in Delgratia Mining Corp. filed a class action suit against the company alleging it concealed facts about test results for a gold project in southern Nevada, plaintiffs' lawyers said Wednesday.
The lawyers said they would seek damages in the case, but did not disclose a dollar amount.
The suit was filed in U.S. District Court in New York on behalf of investors who bought Delgratia common stock and warrants from Nov. 18, 1996, through May 19, 1997, the lawyers said in a statement.

The filing follows an announcement last week that investors filed a class action suit in Nevada, charging the company misrepresented gold prospects. In May, Delgratia, a Vancouver-based mining company, announced an independent auditor had found evidence of tampering at one of its core samples from a Nevada gold mining property.
No one was immediately available at Delgratia to comment on the case.
On Tuesday, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said it had launched a criminal investigation into Delgratia Mining, over the gold test results.
"It is a white-collar crime investigation," said Special Agent Aurelio Flores of the Las Vegas office of the FBI.
Delgratia had said that its rock samples had been tampered with and Delgratia spokesman John Barr told Canada Press Tuesday the company was "absolutely delighted" by the news of the FBI probe.
Delgratia officials had filed a complaint with the U.S. Attorney's Office, claiming the company was the victim of fraud.

Delgratia's problems began in March, when a Nevada state mining official challenged its claims that its property ther held five million ounces of gold. The company's shares rapidly lost half their value on the Nasdaq stock market.
The stock tumbled again the following month when it was reported that lab tests had been conducted by an unlicensed gold assayer who had been convicted of securities fraud in 1978.
